description: Processing sampled signals with algorithms: the discrete Fourier transform and the FFT, FIR and IIR filter design and realisation, finite word-length effects, multirate systems, spectral estimation and applications to speech, audio and images. Each algorithm is implemented in code and run on real recordings in the browser, so every filter is designed, plotted, heard and measured against its specification.
modelledOn: Oppenheim and Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing
Proakis and Manolakis, Digital Signal Processing: Principles, Algorithms and Applications
Mitra, Digital Signal Processing: A Computer-Based Approach
outcomes: Compute and interpret the DFT, use it for fast convolution and spectral analysis, and explain the effects of windowing and zero padding.
Derive and implement radix-2 FFT algorithms and analyse their computational cost.
Design FIR filters by windowing, frequency sampling and equiripple methods, and IIR filters from analogue prototypes, to meet a specification.
Realise filters in direct, cascade, parallel and lattice structures and assess finite word-length effects.
Design decimators, interpolators and polyphase filter banks for multirate systems.
Apply DSP techniques to speech, audio and image processing problems and evaluate the results quantitatively.

units.title: Discrete-time signals, sampling and quantisation
topics: Review of discrete-time signals, LTI systems, convolution, the DTFT and the z-transform
Analogue-to-digital and digital-to-analogue conversion; sampling and reconstruction in practice
Uniform quantisation, quantisation noise and SNR per bit; dithering
Fixed-point and floating-point number formats for DSP

units.title: The discrete Fourier transform
topics: The discrete Fourier series and the DFT as samples of the DTFT; the DFT matrix
DFT properties: linearity, circular shift, symmetry, Parseval's theorem
Circular convolution and computing linear convolution with the DFT; zero padding
Block convolution for long signals: overlap-add and overlap-save
The discrete cosine transform and energy compaction

units.title: The fast Fourier transform
topics: Computational cost of the direct DFT; the divide-and-conquer idea
Radix-2 decimation-in-time and decimation-in-frequency FFTs; butterflies, bit reversal and in-place computation
Mixed-radix and real-input FFTs; the inverse FFT
The Goertzel algorithm and detecting DTMF keypresses on a phone line
Implementing an FFT from scratch and validating it against a library routine

units.title: FIR filter design
topics: Filter specifications: passband, stopband, ripple, transition width; linear phase and the four FIR types
Window method: rectangular, Hann, Hamming, Blackman and Kaiser windows
Frequency-sampling design
Optimal equiripple design with the Parks-McClellan algorithm
FIR structures: direct form, transposed form, cascade and lattice
Removing 50 Hz mains interference and baseline wander from an ECG recording

units.title: IIR filter design
topics: Analogue prototypes: Butterworth, Chebyshev types I and II, and elliptic filters
Impulse invariance and the bilinear transform with frequency prewarping
Frequency transformations to high-pass, band-pass and band-stop filters
IIR structures: direct forms I and II, transposed forms, cascade of second-order sections, parallel form
Finite word-length effects: coefficient quantisation, round-off noise, overflow, scaling and limit cycles
Choosing between FIR and IIR: phase, cost, stability and latency

units.title: Multirate processing
topics: Downsampling and upsampling in time and frequency
Decimation and interpolation filters; rational sampling-rate conversion
Polyphase decomposition and efficient multirate implementations
Two-channel filter banks, quadrature mirror filters and perfect reconstruction
Oversampling and sigma-delta converters

units.title: Spectral analysis
topics: Spectral analysis with the DFT: leakage, resolution, windowing and zero padding
The short-time Fourier transform and spectrograms; time-frequency trade-offs
Random signals: autocorrelation and power spectral density
Non-parametric estimation: periodogram, Bartlett and Welch methods
Parametric estimation: autoregressive models and the Yule-Walker equations
Analysing grid frequency fluctuations and vibration from a cocoa-processing motor

units.title: Optimal and adaptive filtering
topics: Linear prediction and the Levinson-Durbin recursion
The Wiener filter and the mean-square error criterion
Adaptive filters: LMS and normalised LMS; convergence and step size
Noise and echo cancellation for voice calls

units.title: Audio and image processing applications
topics: Speech analysis: pitch detection, linear predictive coding and MFCC features for recognising Twi and Ewe keywords
Audio effects and equalisers; perceptual audio coding principles
Two-dimensional signals: the 2-D DFT and 2-D convolution
Image filtering: smoothing, sharpening, edge detection and median filtering
DCT-based image compression and JPEG for low-bandwidth delivery
Real-time constraints: latency, buffering and DSP processor architectures

schedule.title: Sampling, quantisation and number formats
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute the SNR of a 12-bit converter, the sample rate needed for a 4 kHz speech band, and the error of a Q15 fixed-point multiply.

tasks.title: Quantise a sine wave with 3, 6 and 10 bits, plot the error, and read off the signal-to-noise ratio for each
Sample a two-tone signal below and above its Nyquist rate, plot the reconstruction in each case, and identify the aliased frequency
Implement a fixed-point (Q15) FIR filter in code, compare its output with floating point, and report the error and the overflow cases found

schedule.title: The DFT and circular convolution
schedule.exercise: Compute an 8-point DFT by hand with the DFT matrix, check Parseval's theorem, and show with a small example how circular convolution differs from linear convolution.

tasks.title: Compute the 8-point DFT of a short sequence using the DFT matrix and plot its magnitude spectrum
Compute a linear convolution of two sequences through zero-padded DFTs and confirm it matches direct convolution to numerical precision
Verify linearity, circular shift, symmetry and Parseval's theorem numerically on random signals, and report the largest error for each property

schedule.title: Block convolution and the DCT
schedule.exercise: Estimate the number of multiplications for filtering a 10-minute audio file with a 512-tap filter directly versus overlap-add, and pick a block size.

tasks.title: Compute the DCT of an eight-sample ramp and show how much energy sits in the first two coefficients
Filter a long signal with overlap-add using FFT blocks and verify the output equals direct convolution
Compare overlap-save and direct convolution runtime for filter lengths from 16 to 1024, and find the crossover length

schedule.title: The fast Fourier transform
schedule.exercise: Draw the 8-point radix-2 decimation-in-time flow graph, mark the twiddle factors and bit-reversed inputs, and count multiplications against the direct DFT.

tasks.title: Work through an 8-point decimation-in-time butterfly by hand with twiddle factors and compare the result with the direct DFT
Detect the DTMF keypress digits in a synthesised phone tone with the Goertzel algorithm at the eight standard frequencies
Implement a radix-2 FFT from scratch, validate it against a library on random inputs, and plot runtime against length to confirm n log n

schedule.title: FIR filter design
schedule.exercise: Design a low-pass FIR filter with a 3 kHz cut-off at 16 kHz sampling using a Hamming window, and compare it with a rectangular window design.

tasks.title: Read passband ripple, stopband attenuation and transition width from a plotted filter response and state whether it meets a given specification
Design low-pass FIR filters with rectangular, Hann, Hamming and Blackman windows of 41 taps and compare their stopband attenuation
Design a filter by frequency sampling to meet a given mask, and adjust the transition samples until the stopband ripple falls below 40 dB

schedule.title: Optimal FIR design and ECG clean-up
schedule.exercise: Short report: compare window and equiripple designs for the same specification in terms of order and ripple, and recommend one for a battery-powered ECG monitor.

tasks.title: Draw the direct and transposed forms of a 5-tap FIR filter and compute its output for a short input
Design an equiripple low-pass filter with the Parks-McClellan method and show it needs fewer taps than a Hamming design for the same mask
Remove 50 Hz mains hum and baseline wander from a supplied noisy ECG with FIR filters, and verify the heart-rate peaks are preserved

schedule.title: IIR filter design
schedule.exercise: Design a second-order Butterworth low-pass by the bilinear transform with prewarping at a chosen cut-off, and verify the pole locations are inside the unit circle.

tasks.title: Plot the magnitude responses of fourth-order Butterworth, Chebyshev I and elliptic prototypes and compare their roll-off and ripple
Convert an analogue Butterworth prototype to a digital filter with the bilinear transform and prewarping, and verify its cut-off frequency
Design a band-stop IIR filter that removes a 50 Hz hum from a 1 kHz sampled signal, and check the notch depth and passband flatness

schedule.title: IIR structures and finite word length
schedule.exercise: Compare cascaded second-order sections with a single high-order direct form for a given filter, explaining how coefficient rounding moves the poles.

tasks.title: Draw direct form I and II structures for a second-order IIR filter and compute the first eight output samples for an impulse input
Quantise the coefficients of a sixth-order IIR filter to 8 and 12 bits in direct form and in cascade, and compare the pole shifts
Choose between an FIR and an IIR filter for a 1 kHz low-pass on a 20 kHz sensor stream under a limit of 50 multiplications per sample

schedule.title: Multirate signal processing
schedule.exercise: Design the decimation chain to reduce a 48 kHz audio signal to 8 kHz, specifying the anti-aliasing filter, and compute the saving from a polyphase form.

tasks.title: Downsample a 1 kHz and a 5 kHz tone by 4 at 16 kHz sampling and plot spectra to show which one aliases
Convert a signal from 44.1 kHz to 48 kHz by rational resampling and check the tone frequencies and level are preserved
Build a two-channel QMF filter bank, split and rebuild a test signal, and measure the reconstruction error against perfect reconstruction

schedule.title: Spectral analysis and random signals
schedule.exercise: Spectral analysis lab note: show how window choice and zero padding change the resolved peaks of two tones 20 Hz apart, and state the resolution limit.

tasks.title: Take the DFT of a sine that is not periodic in the window, observe the leakage, and then apply a Hann window to reduce it
Compute a spectrogram of a chirp signal with two window lengths and describe the time-frequency trade-off
Estimate the autocorrelation and power spectral density of noisy sensor data and identify the hidden periodic component

schedule.title: Power spectrum estimation and real signals
schedule.exercise: Compare the periodogram, Welch and AR spectrum estimates for a short noisy record, reporting variance, resolution and model order choices.

tasks.title: Compute the periodogram of a noisy 120 Hz tone and then the Welch estimate, and compare the noise floor smoothness
Fit an autoregressive model with the Yule-Walker equations to a signal and compare its spectrum with the periodogram
Estimate the grid frequency drift from a supplied voltage recording near 50 Hz and detect the motor vibration lines in a cocoa-processing dataset

schedule.title: Linear prediction and adaptive filtering
schedule.exercise: Derive the normal equations of the Wiener filter for a two-tap case and compute the optimal weights from given correlations.

tasks.title: Solve the Wiener normal equations for a two-tap filter from given autocorrelation and cross-correlation values and compute the minimum error
Run the Levinson-Durbin recursion to predict a speech frame, and compare the prediction error energy at orders 4, 8 and 12
Build an LMS adaptive noise canceller for a voice call, tune the step size, and plot convergence for a stable and a diverging setting

schedule.title: Speech, audio and image processing
schedule.exercise: Mini-project proposal: describe the steps from microphone to features to classifier for recognising five Twi or Ewe spoken keywords, including sample rate and frame length.

tasks.title: Filter a noisy grey-scale image with a 3 by 3 mean filter and a median filter, and compare the removal of salt-and-pepper noise
Extract MFCC features from five recorded keywords and compare feature distances between repeats of the same word and different words
Compress a grey-scale image with 8 by 8 DCT blocks at three quantisation levels and report the file size ratio against the image quality
